title: Ivo and the Asset
premise: Noor Vane, an interpreter for a failing peace delegation in the city of Vessengard, receives a burner phone whose caller sounds exactly like her brother Ivo—declared dead twelve years ago. The voice belongs to 'the Asset,' a man surgically rebuilt and trained by the very intelligence service that erased Ivo, and who now carries proof that the peace talks are a staged prelude to a border war three governments need. Hunted by an assassin named Corven and betrayed by her own delegation, Noor must smuggle the Asset and his evidence out of the country, discovering along the way that Ivo's death was the price of her career and that the inheritance her family left her was never money—it was the truth. In the end, Noor chooses exposure over survival, broadcasting the evidence at the cost of the delegation, her immunity, and nearly her life, while the Asset, finally choosing to be Ivo again, disappears into the world he was never meant to rejoin.
about_author: Mara Vane is a former conference interpreter who spent a decade working behind glass in rooms where wars were politely postponed. She writes thrillers about the people who translate power and are never meant to be seen.

chapters.title: The Glass Room
chapters.summary: POV Noor. During a tense delegation session in Vessengard, Noor translates a threat disguised as a compliment, sensing the talks are theater. She notices a delegate's aide photographing her, not the room. Emotional beat: the quiet dread of someone who realizes she is being watched by her own side.

chapters.title: A Number That Should Be Retired
chapters.summary: POV Noor. At her apartment, a cheap burner phone rings; the caller's voice is her dead brother Ivo's, reciting a childhood code phrase. He says only: 'Don't trust the twelfth floor,' then the line dies. Emotional beat: grief cracked open by impossible hope.

chapters.title: Protocol for the Dead
chapters.summary: POV Noor. She investigates Ivo's official death file and finds the signature of her own delegation's security chief, Aldous Renk. Her inquiries trigger a quiet flag on her credentials. Emotional beat: the vertigo of discovering the rules she served were written by liars.

chapters.title: The Twelfth Floor
chapters.summary: POV Renk. The delegation's security chief learns the Asset has gone off-script and that a burner has been activated. He orders Noor surveilled, not arrested—yet. Emotional beat: cold institutional menace; Renk believes he is the reasonable man.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Following the phone's instructions to a flooded tram depot, she meets the caller: a scarred man with Ivo's voice and no Ivo in his face. He carries a drive of intercepted communications. Emotional beat: horror and tenderness colliding in the same breath.

chapters.title: What They Made
chapters.summary: POV the Asset. He recounts, in fragments, twelve years of retraining: new face, new name, new loyalties—and the one thing they couldn't overwrite, a brother's lullaby. He explains the drive contains proof the talks are cover for a planned incursion. Emotional beat: a man arguing with his own reflection.

chapters.title: Corven
chapters.summary: POV Corven. The assassin assigned to retrieve the Asset arrives in Vessengard and reads the city like a ledger, noting that Noor is the variable his employers underestimated. Emotional beat: professional calm stretched over a first hairline crack of doubt.

chapters.title: The Interpreter's Dilemma
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Back in session, she is asked to mistranslate a key clause and refuses, quietly, by translating it true. Renk watches her do it. Emotional beat: the first open act of rebellion, small enough to deny, large enough to be fatal.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Noor and the Asset, alternating. Hiding in a church archive, they decode the drive and find her family name in the original orders—her father's inheritance was the operation itself. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as betrayal, and a fragile partnership forming.

chapters.title: The Aide
chapters.summary: POV Noor. She confronts the aide who photographed her and discovers a second faction inside the delegation that wants the talks to fail for its own reasons. An offer is made: give them the drive, live. Emotional beat: the seduction of the lesser betrayal.

chapters.title: Twelve Floors Down
chapters.summary: POV Renk. Renk meets Corven and realizes the assassin's contract comes from above his own pay grade. He begins quietly building an exit for himself, burning files. Emotional beat: a loyalist discovering loyalty was always a rental agreement.

chapters.title: The Lullaby
chapters.summary: POV Noor. A near-capture at a border checkpoint; the Asset hums the lullaby to steady her hands on the wheel. They cross into the countryside with half the drive copied. Emotional beat: intimacy forged in fear; the brother surfacing inside the Asset.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Lie
chapters.summary: POV the Asset. In a safehouse he lays out the full architecture: each government needs the war for domestic reasons, and the peace delegation exists to give it a deniable funeral. Noor realizes exposure means destroying her own life's work. Emotional beat: the price of truth made explicit.

chapters.title: What Corven Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Corven. Corven corners them at a rail yard but hesitates when the Asset uses a name from Corven's own erased past—a fellow graduate. He lets them run and reports a miss. Emotional beat: the assassin's first act of insubordination, disguised as failure.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Renk summons her privately: confess to espionage, name the Asset as a foreign operative, and be pardoned. He reveals her father helped design the program—her inheritance was tuition. Emotional beat: temptation weaponized through family.

chapters.title: Burn the Delegation
chapters.summary: POV Noor and the Asset. They plan the impossible: broadcast the drive during the signing ceremony, using the delegation's own translation feed. The second faction offers help—for a cut of the leverage. Emotional beat: turning the machine of the talks against their authors.

chapters.title: Renk's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Renk. Renk, cornered by his superiors, decides the only way out is to be the man who helped expose it all. He leaves Noor a door unlocked and a floor plan. Emotional beat: a coward's redemption, purchased cheap and late.

chapters.title: The Signing
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Ceremony day. Wearing her interpreter's badge like armor, Noor reaches the booth; Corven is in the hall, Renk's door is watched, and the feed is one switch away. Emotional beat: terror transposed into perfect professional stillness.

chapters.title: Simultaneous
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Mid-speech, she patches the drive into the live translation feed; the delegates hear the intercepted war orders in three languages at once. Corven reaches the booth and, instead of firing, seals the door behind her. Emotional beat: the climax—truth detonating in the room built to bury it.

chapters.title: Aftermath in Three Languages
chapters.summary: POV Noor. The talks collapse; warrants bloom like weeds. Renk testifies to save himself; the second faction spins; Noor is stripped of immunity and detained. Emotional beat: victory that feels like loss, and the strange lightness of having nothing left to protect.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't Ivo
chapters.summary: POV the Asset. Before the net closes, Corven—settling his own account—moves him out of the country. On the plane, the Asset chooses a name: not Ivo, not the Asset, something new. Emotional beat: identity as a decision rather than an inheritance.

chapters.title: Interpreter, Freelance
chapters.summary: POV Noor, epilogue. Months later, Noor works small honest jobs for journalists and tribunals, unlicensed and unbothered. A postcard arrives with no signature, only a hummed lullaby rendered in musical notation. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope—truth survived, and so, somehow, did they.
